director.chapterArc: A shift from collective labor to intimate revelation: Rook's identity reveal (Elias Marsh), Milo's posthumous recognition as Kindled, and Toren's internal release of his counting compulsion.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational distance. The emotional weight is in the silence between words, not the volume. Do not dramatize Rook's confession; treat it as a factual accounting delivered with exhaustion. Milo's recognition must feel like a quiet truth settling into place, not a climax.

cues.delivery: Grounded observation of the ruined structure. Rook's voice is flat and weary.
cues.from: "I know." Rook was sitting on the coping of the low wall with his left forearm across his knee and his face the colour of the brick behind him. "Look at what you're sitting in the middle of."
cues.through: Three storeys of dark brick with the roof gone, and the bottom of it full of rubble.

cues.delivery: Rook's speech is measured and analytical. He speaks of Milo with a mix of pride and regret, but without sentimentality.
cues.from: "I knew him thirty-four days," said Rook.
cues.through: "And he did the arithmetic on that bank on his own account, at fourteen, in the dark, and he got it right. It was right. I have been over it eleven times since four this morning looking for the place where it was wrong and there isn't one. The road opened because he opened it. The cart went through because he made it go through. Every single person standing at this brick heap is standing here because of what a boy worked out on a low wall at half past three in the morning and did not ask anybody's permission for."
cues.reason: The core revelation about Milo's agency must land as fact.

cues.delivery: A moment of genuine vulnerability. Rook admits his own limitation in this specific ritual.
cues.from: "I'm no good at this," he said.
cues.through: "I'm no good at this," he said.
cues.reason: Humanizes the mentor figure without breaking character.

cues.delivery: Dessa's delivery is precise and dutiful. She carries the weight of Milo's final command.
cues.through: "That's the order now," said Dessa. "It's not mine. I'm only the one carrying it. Come and get it, please."
cues.reason: The ritualistic nature requires a steady, unemotional cadence.

cues.delivery: Intimate and hushed. The revelation of Elias Marsh is a quiet confession, not a shout.
cues.reason: The identity shift must feel like a heavy truth being spoken in the dark.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation of 'Kindled' is instructional but carries the weight of a new philosophy.
cues.from: "Milo Faust was Kindled. That's the word and it's the bottom rung, and it is the only word anybody could honestly put on him, and every single one of you has been carefully not saying it for four weeks and he knew you were doing it and he told Toren so, three hours before the end, in the dark, in a building with no roof.
cues.through: "It never occurred to a single one of the sixty of us that there could be. It has not occurred to me in eleven years. It occurred to me at about a quarter to four yesterday morning, standing on a stone wall, and it is the only thing I have learned in eleven years that Orrin Vell did not teach me."
cues.reason: Clarifies the thematic shift from power to action.

cues.delivery: Amery's final words are delivered with a dry, observational warmth.
cues.through: "It doesn't stop. And it isn't a fault."
cues.reason: A gentle closing to the interaction.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue slows down. The counting becomes a physical act of release.
cues.from: Toren pulled the near shaft with his good arm and did the sums, because the sums were the handrail.
cues.through: It went, the way a number goes when you let it.
cues.reason: The resolution of the chapter is in Toren letting go.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the causal link between Milo's action and their survival.

pauses.after: "I'm no good at this," he said.
pauses.reason: Emotional landing on Rook's admission of inadequacy.

pauses.after: "That's the order now," said Dessa. "It's not mine. I'm only the one carrying it. Come and get it, please."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Dessa completes the ritual instruction.

pauses.after: Toren lay eleven feet away and heard a man say two words out loud on a bank in the dark, and found that his own eyes had gone, and did not move his hands to do anything about it in case he was heard.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Toren's reaction to hearing his name used as Elias Marsh.

pauses.after: There was a silence of about four seconds.
pauses.reason: Pause for the silence of acceptance before Rook agrees.
Emphasis on the specific status being assigned posthumously.

pauses.after: "It doesn't stop. And it isn't a fault."
pauses.reason: Emotional landing on Amery's final wisdom about counting.
Isolating the core truth of Toren's compulsion as a feature, not a bug.
